newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada energy firms get boost from Iraq news.
newsitem.headline: Canada energy firms get boost from Iraq news.

text.p: Investors rushed to buy Canadian oil and gas shares on Tuesday as crude prices climbed on news that the U.N.-Iraq oil-for-food plan was put on hold.
The plan, which was negotiated for months and approved in May, was placed in jeopardy after military action by Baghdad that led to the U.S. cruise missile attack on Iraq early on Tuesday.
The Toronto Stock Exchange's oil and gas index was up 38.76 points at midday to 5388.51 after climbing to an earlier high of 5397.68.
The oils outpaced the key TSE 300 index, which was up just 5.97 points to 5149.40 during Tuesday's session.
NYMEX October crude oil was trading up US$0.86 a barrel to 23.11 on Tuesday.
Peter Linder, analyst with CIBC Wood Gundy, said the likely removal of Iraqi crude from the world market came just as seasonal demand was on the upswing.
"We're going into the heating season. We're going into a situation where demand is strong. Inventories are still quite low and consequently it bodes well for the sector," Linder said.
For many Canadian producers, third-quarter results were already expected to be strong as drilling picked up after a delayed development season in the spring, he said.
The expected boost in production volumes, coupled with high oil prices, should mean even better returns, he said.
Leading the charge upward among large Canadian energy firms was Renaissance Energy Ltd, which gained 0.70 to 39.20 on 337,769 shares.
Renaissance, whose output was expected to include two-thirds oil in 1997, should produce 100,000 barrels a day next year, Linder said.
Linder said Renaissance's booming output led him to raise his 12-month target price for the company to 50 from 45.
"They're drilling very successfully. Oil production is rising rapidly," he said. "So all this good news on the oil side signficantly helps Renaissance."

Another firm with rising output that gained on Tuesday was Canadian Natural Resources Ltd. Canadian Natural, whose oil production jumped after its recent acquisition of Sceptre Resources, was up 0.35 at 28.40.

International producers weighted to crude prices also gained. Gulf Canada Resources Ltd was up 0.15 to 8.25. Canadian Occidental Petroleum Ltd gained 0.25 to 23. Talisman Energy Inc was at 34.25, up 0.40.
